preview_text: Spain topped Group H with nine points, finishing with a 1-0 win over Uruguay in their final group match. Mikel Oyarzabal scored the only goal to secure top spot, continuing a group stage in which Spain scored five goals while conceding none.
Pedri and Alex Baena served as Spain's primary corner kick takers. Lamine Yamal has been a consistent creative force on the right and Dani Olmo provides linking play through the centre of midfield.

Spain kept three clean sheets across the group stage and conceded zero goals, making them one of two teams alongside Mexico to achieve a perfect defensive group stage record. They opened with a 0-0 draw with Cape Verde before winning their final two matches.

Mikel Oyarzabal leads Spain in DFS value with the tournament-clinching goal against Uruguay and the highest opto percentage on the slate among attacking options. Lamine Yamal offers high-ceiling upside as Spain's most direct wide threat.

Austria advanced from Group J in second place after a dramatic 3-3 draw with Algeria in their final group game. Marko Arnautovic opened the scoring and Marcel Sabitzer struck to make it 2-1 before Sasa Kalajdzic headed in an equalizer in the 96th minute to secure qualification.

Marcel Sabitzer served as Austria's corner kick taker and scored in the group stage decider against Algeria. Austria finished with seven points and conceded twice in three group games, with their only loss coming against Argentina.

Austria scored seven goals across the group stage and scored in all three matches. They advanced through a final-minute equalizer at the 96th minute against Algeria — the last goal of any group stage match at this tournament.

Marcel Sabitzer is the top Austria DFS option with a group stage goal and corner kick volume as the team's primary set piece delivery source. Marko Arnautovic provides forward goal threat at a mid-range salary.

Portugal advanced from Group K in second place behind Colombia, going unbeaten through a draw with DR Congo, a 5-0 win over Uzbekistan, and a goalless draw with Colombia in a dead rubber. Cristiano Ronaldo scored twice against Uzbekistan to lead the team in goals.

Bruno Fernandes and Nuno Mendes served as Portugal's corner kick takers throughout the group stage, with Mendes also contributing a goal in the tournament. Joao Neves has already scored at this World Cup from midfield.

Portugal registered a 5-0 demolition of Uzbekistan as their marquee group stage result, with Ronaldo scoring twice and multiple different players contributing. They are unbeaten in the tournament and carry the deepest attacking squad in this half of the bracket.

Cristiano Ronaldo leads Portugal in DFS value with two group stage goals and the highest opto share among all forward options on the slate. Bruno Fernandes provides corner kick volume and creative output at a salary below the top-tier forwards.

Croatia advanced from Group L in second place after wins over Panama and Ghana, recovering from an opening 4-2 loss to England. Petar Sucic scored against Ghana and Nikola Vlasic headed in a late winner as Croatia sealed second place with a 2-1 result.

Luka Modric became the oldest player in World Cup history to register an assist during the Ghana match, setting up Vlasic's winner. Ivan Perisic and Martin Baturina served as Croatia's corner kick takers throughout the group stage.

Croatia scored five goals across their three group games from five different scorers, the broadest goal distribution of any team advancing from the round. Their 4-2 defeat to England in Round 1 was their only loss, and the two wins that followed came by single goals.

Ante Budimir leads Croatia in DFS opto as the primary striker and focal point of the attack. Ivan Perisic provides corner kick volume and attacking width at left back, while Nikola Vlasic offers upside off his game-winning header against Ghana.

Switzerland topped Group B with seven points, sealing first place with a 2-1 win over Canada in their final group game. Ruben Vargas and Johan Manzambi both scored as Switzerland came from behind to win after conceding early.

Ruben Vargas and Ricardo Rodriguez served as Switzerland's corner kick takers throughout the group stage. Breel Embolo leads the attack as the primary striker and carried the highest projected ownership throughout the tournament.

Switzerland scored eight goals across three group games and won all three matches, the best record of any European side remaining in the tournament. They conceded four goals but never lost the lead for long in any of their three matches.

Breel Embolo anchors Switzerland's DFS output as the highest-opto player on the slate with the most projected minutes at striker. Ruben Vargas provides a corner kick delivery pivot at a salary below the top-tier forwards.

Algeria qualified for the Round of 32 as one of the best third-placed teams after a dramatic 3-3 draw with Austria in their final group game. Rafik Belghali scored a brilliant individual goal before halftime, and Riyad Mahrez struck in the 93rd minute before being denied a winner by Kalajdzic's 96th-minute equalizer.

Riyad Mahrez and Fares Chaibi served as Algeria's corner kick takers. Algeria beat Jordan in Round 2 with Mahrez and Gouiri among the key contributors, and Mahrez leads the team with the most goal involvement in the tournament.

Algeria scored in all three group games despite losing to Argentina 3-0 in their opener. Their final group game against Austria produced six goals and two stoppage-time strikes. Mahrez has been involved in most of their attacking moments as the team's primary creator.

Riyad Mahrez leads Algeria in DFS value with corner kick volume and a tournament goal in the Austria thriller. Amine Gouiri offers forward goal upside at a mid-range salary as Algeria's primary striker option.
